title: Adaptive per-region lease circuit and spillover observability dashboard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create instrumentation and a set of dashboards for the new per-region lease-based circuit controller. The controller issues short-lived 'congestion leases' on overloaded tenants/paths to coordinate regional admission gating and enable graceful multi-region spillover. We need golden-signal metrics, token-level latency SLIs, expose lease state transitions, and build dashboards and alerts for on-call and SREs.
background: We currently use coarse circuit breakers based on aggregated admit rates which cause noisy failovers and frequent flapping during microbursts. The new lease approach introduces timeboxed admission holds (leases) scoped to region+shard+route to reduce oscillation and give routing layers deterministic windows to redirect traffic. This ticket ties the controller to observability and SLO enforcement so ops can understand why a lease was granted and whether failover succeeded.
proposed_solution: Instrument the controller and runtime to emit these canonical signals: lease_granted, lease_released, admit_decision, queue_depth, admitted_tokens, rejected_tokens, kv_cache_hit, token_latency_histogram (per-token), decode_queue_ms, model_kernel_wait_ms, and route_spillover_event. Build Grafana dashboards and a compact on-call playbook: show current lease map, lease duration histograms, p50/p95/p99 token latency by region and route, admitted vs rejected tokens over time, and spillover routing effectiveness (requests routed vs successful responses). Wire alerts for prolonged leases, high rejected_token ratios, and SLO breach conditions computed from token-level SLIs. Add synthetic probe rows to validate end-to-end behavior and link to canary tester.
metrics: lease_granted_total (counter) - tags: region, shard, route, model
admit_decision{admit, reject, delayed} (counter) - tags: region, route, tenant_tier
token_latency_ms (histogram) - tags: region, route, model, prefix_length
dashboard_panels: Lease map (table) - active leases with TTL, owner, and reason
Lease lifecycle timeline - stacked events per-region showing grant->renew->release
Lease duration distribution - histogram with p50/p90/p99
Token-level latency heatmap - region x prefix_length buckets (p50/p95/p99)
Admit vs Reject trend - timeseries of counters with rate per minute
Rejected token ratio by tenant - bar chart with severity coloring
Spillover effectiveness - % of routed requests that completed within SLA after reroute
KV cache hit vs token latency scatter - correlate cache effectiveness with tail latency
Decode queue and kernel wait timelines - show source of backpressure
Synthetic probe rows - last successful probe latency and failure reason
acceptance_criteria: All metrics and events listed in "metrics" and "telemetry_events" are emitted from controller/runtime and available in metrics/trace platform
Dashboards exist in Grafana with panels described under "dashboard_panels" and sensible defaults for 1h/6h/24h ranges
On-call alerts: lease_age > 2x median and rejected_token_ratio > 2% for 5m triggers pager; documented in playbook
Token-level SLI: instrumented token_latency_ms histogram is used to compute p95 token latency SLI per-route and is visible in dashboard
Synthetic canary triggers simulated regional overload and confirms lease grant, spillover, and recovery; results logged in dashboard

blockers: Need increased cardinality allowance for lease_id tag in metrics backend (cost approval pending)
Routing layer currently lacks a durable lease cache for cross-region coordination; depends on infra change INF-314
notes: We intentionally use short leases (1s-10s) to avoid long holds that mask upstream congestion signals.
Lease grants include a small randomized jitter to reduce synchronized renewals across shards.
Token-level SLIs should be computed from histogram buckets with consistent exemplar sampling to allow trace links back to request_id.
When designing alerts, prefer multi-bucket confirmation (e.g., lease_age + rejected_ratio) to reduce false positives during infra restarts.
